key_insight: Orchestrating small, open-weight language models with evidence-grounded workflows can outperform single-model baselines for malware detonation report analysis.
engineering_relevance: This suggests practical, lower-cost malware triage systems can be built with deployable small models instead of relying on expensive closed frontier LLMs.
method: Benchmarked 11 open-weight SLMs, 3 cyber-security pre-trained models, and 6 frontier LLMs on the CyberSecEval Malware Analysis benchmark.
Compared four orchestration designs: multi-agent evidence collection, adversarial debate, hierarchical consultation, and a hybrid grounded-plus-debate system.
Evaluated accuracy on structured questions about filesystem, network, and process behaviors from malware detonation reports.
evidence_signal: The hybrid Qwen3-4B + Foundation-Sec-8B system reached 35.30% accuracy, beating the strongest cyber-specialized baseline (22.54%) and the strongest ungrounded frontier baseline (34.77%), while grounded Gemini achieved 38.22% with the same evidence pipeline.
watch_item: Results depend on benchmark quality and evidence-pipeline design, so deployment may be sensitive to report formatting, orchestration overhead, and domain shift.
paper_title: Small, Free, and Effective: Orchestrating Open-Weight Small Language Models to Outperform Single LLM for Malware Analysis
